correctness.rationale: PASS. For the nine-dimensional H_{<=2}, evaluate a south pole, regular 3-ring at height x and regular 5-ring at y. Unit-normalized row discrete Fourier transforms isolate m=±2 on the five-ring; after elimination, m=±1 gives two 2x2 radial Vandermonde blocks, and m=0 gives three heights (-1,x,y). Explicit normalized harmonic coefficients give |det M|²=5189853515625/(1073741824*pi^9)(1+x)^4(1−x)^2(1+y)^8(1−y)^6(y−x)^6; phases cancel in absolute value. Every distinct interior x,y yields invertibility. In each of x<y and y<x, log F is strictly concave and tends to −infinity on chamber boundaries, hence has a unique maximizer. Differentiating yields 6x²−3xy−x+y−3=0 and 7xy−x−10y²+y+3=0, whose interior roots are the two displayed sqrt(2305) pairs. Exact rational bounds show the y<x maximizer dominates the other chamber; unique global solution is x=(11+sqrt(2305))/78,y=3/26−sqrt(2305)/130. Independent normalized complex harmonic determinants for several heights and angular shifts agreed with the closed factorization to ~3e−15; symbolic derivatives and chamber stationary equations were also independently checked. This is global only within the prescribed 1+3+5 architecture, not all nine-point placements.
